title: Soil carbon turnover: the Rothamsted Carbon Model (RothC-26.3)
licence: Numerical values cited as facts with attribution; no text, figures or datasets reproduced.

sources.citation: Coleman, K., Prout, J. M. and Milne, A. E. (February 2024). RothC - A model for the turnover of carbon in soil: Model Description. Rothamsted Research. https://www.rothamsted.ac.uk/sites/default/files/Documents/RothC_description.pdf (sections 1.4-1.7).

items.description: Decomposition rate constants of the four active compartments: decomposable and resistant plant material, microbial biomass and humified organic matter. A compartment holding Y declines to Y exp(-a b c k t) over t years
items.note: Section 1.5: set by tuning to Rothamsted's long-term experiments and 'not normally altered when using the model'.

items.description: Rate modifier for temperature: a = A / (1 + exp(B / (T + C))), T the mean air temperature in degrees C
items.note: Section 1.6, with T the average monthly air temperature.

items.description: Rate modifier for soil cover: vegetated soil decomposes more slowly than bare soil
Ratio of decomposable to resistant plant material in incoming plant carbon, by vegetation; farmyard manure split
items.note: Section 1.3 gives the ratios 1.44 (59% DPM, 41% RPM), 0.67 for unimproved grassland and scrub including savanna, and 0.25 (20% DPM, 80% RPM) for deciduous or tropical woodland; the 0.67 fractions are ratio / (1 + ratio). Farmyard manure is 'more decomposed than normal crop plant material': DPM 49%, RPM 49%, HUM 2%.

items.description: Split of decomposed carbon between CO2 and new BIO + HUM: x = CO2 / (BIO + HUM) = s (p + q exp(-r %clay)); BIO + HUM is then 46% BIO and 54% HUM
items.note: Section 1.7: x = 1.67 (1.85 + 1.60 exp(-0.0786 %clay)); the scaling 1.67 sets x to 3.51 at Rothamsted's 23.4% clay and is used for all soils. Section 1.3: BIO + HUM is split 46% BIO, 54% HUM.
